Poor course conditions,  not really due to the heavy rains but due to a lot of dead grass areas and poor over all maintenance.   I have never seen so many broken tees on tee boxes.   Clean up your course better,  that includes tee boxes.   The starter, John, thought he was something special and was holding up play when the group ahead of us was hitting their third shot onto a part 5, he told us not to hit yet.   I told him if I could hit it that far I'd give him $100.  Then he threatened to kick me off the course.   WHY?  Because I, as a golfer am supposed to keep the pace of play going by staying up with the group ahead of us? But John wanted to act like he was something special and threaten to remove me just because he thought he could.  I worked at that course 45 years ago and I don't need to be treated that way by a starter.  He is just a starter.   Stay in your lane and and allow the players to maintain the pace of play.  After today,  I won't be back and will take my money elsewhere.

Pace of play is brutal, and to make it worse, the marshals come around yelling at you to speed up… while you’re literally stuck behind 4–5 groups with nowhere to go. Makes zero sense.

Course conditions don’t make up for it either. Fairways are bumpy and inconsistent, and the greens are just mediocre at best. Nothing about the setup or upkeep justifies the price.

Only positive is the ladies in the pro shop were nice, but that doesn’t make up for paying $91 for 18 with a cart. That’s borderline robbery for the experience you get here. Would not come back.

Kennedy Golf Course is a solid 4-star option for getting a round in around Denver. The staff in the pro shop and around the clubhouse are consistently friendly and welcoming, which sets a good tone for the day. Another major upside is the pricing on concessions; the food and drinks are refreshingly cheap, making it easy to grab a quick bite or a beer without overspending.

The reason it holds at 4 stars is that the actual course conditions can be quite variable depending on when you play. You might encounter some rough patches or inconsistent greens from time to time. However, given the overall value, the affordable amenities, and the laid-back atmosphere, it remains a reliable and enjoyable spot to tee it up.

The Poor Orphan of Denver City Courses - At $83 (riding) Kennedy is a questionable value for a Sunday round of golf. It is far inferior to the other Denver city courses such as City Park and Willis Case. The carts are old and crappy, many with cigarette burns in the seats. The facilities are old and run down, the parking lot is rutted and cracked. The course itself is in dire need of a facelift. It needs new tees with additional tee boxes and some real differentiation between its tees. The three strengths that the course has is its people, staff are friendly and helpful, the course conditions (quite good) and the fact that you can usually get a tee time (probably due to the negative factors listed above). All in all a wasted resource for Denver golf - I hope they have plans to address in the future.

I’ve never been treated so badly by staff at a golf course than how I was today at this place. You could not pay me enough money to come back to be treated this way.

We were at our tee on time and were told that I couldn’t golf because we each needed to have our own set of clubs (I’ve always played on my boyfriend’s clubs for years, that is what I’m used to and have practiced with). So we went up to the pro shop and we asked if that was a rule just here because we have never heard of that before, and I have worked at a golf course before. We were just curious because logically it didn’t make sense but we were also wondering if that’s what we need to expect just here or in Colorado since we recently moved here. We’ve golfed in 5 different states and had never heard of this rule. The pro shop woman cut us off 4 times and rudely said “Sweetheart that is a rule everywhere you go”. Obviously that is not the case since I’ve always used my boyfriend’s clubs. We play best ball because I’m not the best, so I didn’t understand their reasoning on how each of us having two sets of clubs makes it go quicker, especially when we had a cart. When we played I obviously still used my boyfriend’s better clubs that I’ve been using for 5 years. So it was really just a scam at the end of the day so they can get more money out of people, but we didn’t object to it and complied with everything. Just merely we’re trying to figure out if this was just a rule at their golf course. 2 members overhead what went on in the pro shop and came up to talk to us afterwards. They stated that the course was beautiful but prices are going up and management is going down and the only reason why they still golf there is that they have golfed there since they were young. They apologized a bunch of times for the golf course employees and said the course really is a good course and they hoped we could still enjoy our time but said they did not blame us if we did not come back. So we go back to our tee 10 minutes late, which made everyone else irritated because the golf course caused a backup in the schedule. Then to top it off - a older woman walks up to our cart and doesn’t say anything, she circled our cart looking at us and then walked back to the other ambassador and started whispering. Then they both came back and circled our cart again. It felt like we were getting absolutely harassed because we had questions while complying with their rules. Another member who ended up playing with us because the schedule was messed up was blown away that they made us rent when they don’t make him to do that with his children.

Yes it does say on their website each person needed their own set of clubs, but it is tucked away in their website. And again, even though it didn’t make sense that was not the issue. The issue was that they treated us like we had never golfed before and were very rude. I’ve worked at a golf course and luckily this wasn’t my first time golfing by any means, but if it was, today would be enough to make me never want to golf again.

Kennedy is a fantastic Denver course for a few reasons, and it's not 5 stars for a few others.

The 27 hole layout is effectively set up for most skill levels:
West 9 is great for high handicappers as there is zero water and just enough trees to punish you, but enough room to escape and still score well. Decent length if you play the tips

Babe Lind: mid to high handicappers have an opportunity to score really well depending on how they pay the holes with water. Water only should come into play on two holes, but the second tee box is set to drive over a fairly wide cherry creek section.
Hole six is the toughest to score because you need to layup but still looking at a 200-225 yard approach. I've only hit GIR once in over a dozen attempts no matter how well I plan it. It's fun though.

Then you have the really long par 5, 600 yards from the tips. Easy par 5, very forgiving

8 is really the only hole that water comes into play if you pull your drive bad and really smash it. Really fun combination of length and interesting par 4 layouts.

Both these 9 end right at the clubhouse, which is satisfactory.

Creek: low handicappers and mid can score well (but you better be on that day if you are a mid handicapper) my favorite but the most difficult and least forgiving, by far, with water playing a real role for bad scoring on 4 holes. Fairways are narrow and many run near the creek, but it's a great course. Less views than the other two but it's more intimate and beautiful while playing the actual course.

The most challenging is hole 9 because of it's design. You need to lay up but if you can carry 265 you can drive it from the gold tees. Good luck on the tips.

The greens are usually well enough kept to keep returning. Tee boxes are on par with the price. Fairways are usually fine. But the biggest issue I have is with the lack of twilight+cart at a reasonable time. No carts on twilight unlike meadow hills. Price could be better. Often plays slow because most novice golfers don't accept how much they suck and they take FOREVER! even with the sometimes slow play, it's a great place to play all 27. I'd recommend starting at babe Lind to Creek, get your mojo and then go play darn near scratch at West.

I saw 3 yardage markers in 18 holes, (really bad day to forget my Garmin).  The sad part is the fixes would not take much effort or expense. Some paint, new signage, remodel and lighting in the clubhouse would be cheap and easy.
